title: Tanaris
body: Tanaris is a sea of shifting sand in the far southeast of Kalimdor. Trolls ruled it long ago, and their ruins lie half buried among the dunes; the Sandfury still hold the walled city of Zul'Farrak. The goblins of the Steamwheedle Cartel have made the rest their business, though nomads hold most of Gadgetzan's wells and pirates prey on its ships. Older powers lie deeper in: silithid hives drain the desert pools, giants walk before the sealed gates of Uldum, and in the eastern mountains the bronze dragonflight keeps the Caverns of Time.

title: Gadgetzan
body: Gadgetzan is the Steamwheedle Cartel's chief town in Kalimdor, a walled goblin settlement among the dunes, and like every cartel town it is neutral ground: anyone with coin is welcome, and the bruisers fall hard on whoever starts trouble. Water is its lifeblood and its biggest business, and the Gadgetzan Water Company frets over every well, for the Wastewander nomads have seized the field of water towers east of town that keeps it alive.

title: Steamwheedle Port
body: Steamwheedle Port is the cartel's harbor on the northeastern coast, where ships run to and from Booty Bay. Among the goblins live a few odd scholars: an old troll mystic, Yeh'kinya, who studies an ancient god he will not yet name, and just north of the port the gnome Narain Soothfancy, who calls himself a psychic and rarely guesses right.

parts.body: Yeh'kinya's god is Hakkar the Soulflayer, whose return the trolls foretell, some as glory for their race, others as the end of all things.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Steamwheedle_Port (east coast port, road to Gadgetzan, residents)

parts.body: Yeh'kinya served Hakkar all along. The egg he was brought was a cradle, not a prison, and he gloats that the Soulflayer is already reborn in Zul'Gurub.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Steamwheedle_Port (east coast port, road to Gadgetzan, residents)

parts.body: Behind the bluster Narain is a gifted engineer: the blue dragon Azuregos calls him a terrible, terrible psychic but an amazing engineer.

title: Caverns of Time
body: In the mountains of eastern Tanaris a great cavern opens into the realm of Nozdormu, the Timeless One, where the bronze dragonflight has watched over the flow of time since the world was young. Before the entrance stands Anachronos, heir of Nozdormu, in his true dragon form. He speaks as though a war were close at hand: this time, he insists, the first strike must be theirs, so that the mistakes of the past are not repeated.

parts.body: Now the flight receives mortal visitors. Below, tunnels called timeways lead into moments of history, and strange beings are trying to unmake them while Nozdormu is away.
The keepers name the culprits: a malevolent order called the Infinite Dragonflight, which would change time on a grand scale.

title: Zul'Farrak
body: In the northwest of Tanaris rise the walls of Zul'Farrak, city of the Sandfury trolls, sand trolls steeped in dark magic who attack anyone who comes near and guard the rare open water of Sandsorrow Watch to the east. Legends cling to the place: a hydra god, Gahz'rilla, is said to dwell in a sacred pool within its walls, and the smith Trenton Lighthammer of Gadgetzan still remembers with dread the warband that once marched out of it.

title: The Gaping Chasm
body: Southeast of Gadgetzan the desert splits open into the Gaping Chasm, a hive of the Hazzali silithid, its mounds boiling with wasps and swarmers while workers dig ever deeper below. The Gadgetzan Water Company long waved off reports of strange bugs drinking the desert dry as one more nomad trick, until its surveyors began to meet them; its top assistant, Scrimshank, went into the chasm and has not been heard from since.

parts.body: The company's alchemist found the bugs unlike any insect he had ever seen, as if steered by an outside force, and the research points to a third party controlling them.

title: Valley of the Watchers
body: In the far southwest of Tanaris a valley runs between the mountains to a great sealed gate, the entrance to Uldum, a place few believe is more than a myth. The gate cannot be forced, and huge giants walk the valley floor as if keeping watch over it. Before the gate stands a stone pedestal, silent to those who pass it by, and a prospector of the Explorers' League keeps a lonely camp nearby.

parts.body: Before the gates the discs from Uldaman hum and glow, and a stone watcher springs to life: the discs alone are not enough, it says, and the missing Plates of Uldum must be joined to them.
